title: Unified Inference: Product overview, PRD, design spec, roadmap & pricing — Oct 2026
author: Ethan Carter
content:
Executive summary

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design, roadmap & themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference initiative (internal name: UnifiedInference v2026.Q4). Unified Inference is Redwood’s effort to provide a single, predictable developer experience across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments with consistent SLAs, unified routing, and cost controls. The goal for this phase is to stabilize the product feature set for enterprise signups and Dedicated migrations while delivering clear pricing packages and a gradual rollout plan.

Goals and success metrics

Goals (90-day and 12-month):
- 90-day: Launch a GA product bundle for Unified Inference that supports model pinning, routing policies, and cost-aware fallbacks across environments.
- 12-month: Reduce customer unit cost for common enterprise workloads by 20% while maintaining parity in 95th percentile latency with pre-2026 baseline.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Adoption: 25 enterprise customers onboarded to Dedicated or Private enrollment within 6 months of GA.
- Reliability: End-to-end 95th percentile request latency <= 200ms for short-generations (<256 tokens) for Hosted API; error rate <0.5% (customer impacting errors).
- Cost efficiency: Median cost-per-1k-tokens served reduced by 15% for customers using recommended quantization and caching profiles.
- Developer experience: <2 day average time-to-first-successful-inference for new accounts following quickstart.

Product scope and user personas

Primary personas:
- ML engineer (model owner) — wants predictable performance and model versioning/rollouts.
- Backend engineer — wants stable APIs, SDKs, and cost controls.
- Platform engineer (customer infra) — needs Private deployment guides, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
- Product manager / Solutions engineer — needs pricing and migration playbooks for sales.

In-scope features (GA):
- Unified API surface for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking (no breaking changes to existing endpoints).
- Model pinning and model catalog visibility per deployment mode.
- Smart routing engine supporting policy definitions: latency-first, cost-first, region affinity, and fallback chains.
- Built-in prefix KV caching and TTL configuration per route.
- Cost/performance profiles: default quantified suggestions for batching, quantization, and caching.
- Rollout features: per-customer canary (10/50/100), A/B variants, and automatic fallback to cheaper variants.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and rollout dashboards in Redwood Console.

Out of scope for this release:
- New model training or model editing UIs; advanced eval-suite integrations (these remain roadmap items).

PRD: requirements and acceptance criteria

User stories (high level):
1) As an ML engineer, I can pin a model version to a production route and define a rollback policy so that model regressions can be reverted quickly.
   - Acceptance: Pin applied in control plane within 10s; traffic split change completes within configured canary window; audit entry recorded.
2) As a backend engineer, I can declare a routing policy that prefers low-cost variants but fails over to lower-latency variants when 95th percentile exceeds threshold.
   - Acceptance: Policy applied; documented latency & cost tradeoffs visible in Console; fallback occurs automatically when threshold breached.
3) As a platform engineer, I can deploy Redwood Private with an optional customer-managed KMS and verify that logs are shipped to customer SIEM.
   - Acceptance: KMS integration tested; audit logs emitted to configured S3/ELK endpoint; documentation and checklist provided.
4) As a dev using the Hosted API, I can enable prefix caching for a route and observe reduced token usage and cost in Console within 24 hours.
   - Acceptance: Cache hit metrics exposed; cost delta shown; default TTL applied and editable.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- Performance: 95th percentile latency targets: Hosted API <= 200ms for <256 tokens; Dedicated SLA adjustable per contract not to exceed 150ms P95 for reserved small-model workloads.
- Reliability: system availability target 99.95% for Hosted APIs; Dedicated SLA and Private depend on contract.
- Security & compliance: All customer data in transit TLS1.2+; storage encrypted at rest via customer-managed or Redwood-managed KMS; RBAC enforced for model pinning & rollouts.
- Observability: All routes must emit latency, token_count, cost_estimate, and error_type tags. Logs retained per retention policy tier.
- Scalability: Control plane must handle 2000 concurrent route changes per minute in spikes without >500ms median API latency.

Constraints and assumptions:
- We assume standard model compatibility (no model-format translation). Any model requiring custom kernels or unsupported ops will be handled as out-of-band onboarding.
- Customers migrating from self-hosted model infra may require professional services for capacity planning.

Design specification (high level)

Architecture overview:
- Control plane: service for model metadata, routing policy management, rollout orchestration, billing integration, and audit logs.
- Data plane (serving runtime): model execution, KV cache, batching, kernel selection.
- Routing layer: lightweight policy evaluator & decision cache colocated with edge/proxy tier to minimize added latency.
- Observability pipeline: telemetry collector -> metrics store (Prometheus/Thanos) -> Console dashboards; traces to Jaeger; logs to central ELK.

API changes and schema:
- No breaking changes to existing /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints.
- New optional fields in route config:
  - routing_policy: {"strategy": "latency|cost|region|hybrid", "thresholds": {...}}
  - model_pin: "model-id@version"
  - cache_config: {"prefix_enabled": true, "ttl_seconds": 3600, "max_entries": 100000}
  - rollout: {"strategy": "canary|ab", "steps": [{"percent":10,"duration_minutes":30}, ...]}
- Example CLI for rollout: redwood route update --route payments-checkout --model-pin open-llama-7b@v2 --rollout "canary:10@30m,50@60m,100@120m"

Service ownership and component responsibilities:
- Control plane: product + eng-platform (owner: Eng-Platform)
- Routing engine: eng-serving-runtime (owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime)
- Console integrations and dashboards: eng-developer-experience (owner: DevX)
- Dedicated/Private packaging and docs: eng-private-deployments (owner: Private Deployments)

Migration and rollout strategy (customer-facing):
1) Beta: Invite top 10 pilot customers to test model pinning and routing policies. Collect SLO regressions and adjust default thresholds.
2) Gradual GA: Turn on for new Hosted customers, opt-in for existing customers.
3) Dedicated/Private: Offer migration playbook, capacity planning worksheet, and professional services option.

Roadmap and themes (next 4 quarters)

Q4 2026 (this release — GA):
- GA for Unified Inference core features listed above.
- Pricing and packaging published.
- Pilot program for Dedicated migrations.

Q1 2027:
- Eval-driven quality guardrails: integrate evaluation harness into rollout workflows to auto-block regressive model versions.
- Auto-quantization suggestions per workload and model.

Q2 2027:
- Multi-region cross-region routing & drift-aware traffic steering.
- Advanced caching (partial token-level diff caching).

Q3 2027:
- SLO-backed cost optimization engine with automated billing controls and alerts.
- First-class Marketplace for validated model variants and third-party model providers.

Pricing and packaging notes

Principles: transparency, predictable unit economics, and an upsell path from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.

Proposed bundles (GA):
- Hosted API (self-serve)
  - Free tier: 50k tokens/month for evaluation.
  - Pay-as-you-go: $0.XX per 1k tokens for base generation; embedding priced separately.
  - Add-ons: advanced observability retention (monthly), premium support.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity)
  - Base: committed monthly capacity priced by GPU type and target throughput (starting at $X,XXX/month for small instance pools).
  - Includes: reserved throughput SLA, burst pool option, deployment assistance.
  - Overages: metered at a discounted pay-as-you-go rate.
- Private (VPC/on-prem)
  - Licensing model: platform fee + per-node licensing + optional professional services.
  - Security add-ons: HSM/KMS integration, extended audit retention, compliance package.

Example pricing table (illustrative):
- Hosted generation: $0.025 / 1k tokens (base model)
- Hosted embeddings: $0.08 / 1k embeddings units
- Dedicated reserved: $6,000 / month for 4x A10-equivalent reserved pool (example)
- Private license: $30,000 / year + per-node $1,500 / month (example)

Discounts & enterprise negotiations:
- Volume discounts applied by committed spend tiers.
- Migration credits for customers moving from self-hosted (case-by-case).

Release notes — Unified Inference GA (v2026.Q4)

Highlights:
- Unified API: Single interface for generation, chat, embeddings across deployments.
- Routing policies: New control-plane fields for model_pin and routing_policy.
- Rollouts: Canary & A/B rollout support with audit logging.
- KV prefix caching: Per-route configuration with metrics and TTL control.
- Console improvements: per-route cost breakdown and rollout dashboards.

Breaking changes: None. Backwards-compatible additions only.

Migration notes for customers:
- Existing routes without model_pin will continue to use model catalog defaults. Customers wanting deterministic behavior should set model_pin.
- Customers using 3rd-party proxies should ensure request headers used for routing (x-redwood-route-id) are preserved.

Operational readiness checklist (for launch):
- [x] SLA docs finalized and approved by Legal.
- [x] Console dashboards instrumented for KPIs.
- [x] Private deployment packaging tested end-to-end for 3 sample customers.
- [x] Playbooks: migration, rollback, and incident response published.

Monitoring & alerts (key alerts to add):
- P95 latency > 200ms for Hosted API: pager to SRE after 15m sustained.
- Error rate > 0.5% for any route: page on-call and trigger incident review.
- Rollout failure (canary error spike > threshold): auto-rollback and alert product owner.

Ownership and next steps

Owners & contacts:
- Product owner: Ethan Carter (product)
- Eng leads: Leila Morgan (eng-serving-runtime), Diego Alvarez (eng-platform), Priya Shah (devx)

Immediate next steps (2 weeks):
1) Finalize pricing page copy and update public pricing site. (Owner: finance & product)
2) Prepare Dedicated migration playbook & capacity worksheet. (Owner: eng-private-deployments)
3) Run 3 full customer pilots and collect rollout telemetry. (Owner: solutions engineering)
4) Ship first customer-facing migration checklist and enable professional services skus. (Owner: go-to-market)

Rollback plan (if regressions observed post-GA):
1) For Hosted API: trigger automatic fallback to pinned stable variant and rollback rollout.
2) For Dedicated: pause new deployments, migrate traffic to standby capacity or older model variants, notify customers.
3) For Private: follow customer-approved rollback checklist and provide hotfix patch.

Appendix: sample config snippets

Example route JSON (route config):
{
  "route_id": "payments-checkout",
  "model_pin": "open-llama-7b@v2",
  "routing_policy": "{\"strategy\": \"hybrid\", \"thresholds\": {\"p95_latency_ms\": 180}}",
  "cache_config": "{\"prefix_enabled\": true, \"ttl_seconds\": 3600, \"max_entries\": 100000}",
  "rollout": "canary:10@30m,50@60m,100@120m"
}
